title: Take
about: The many meanings of take: take in a physical sense (take apart, take back, take aside, take off), in an abstract sense (take up a hobby, take ten per cent off, take something in) and other common uses such as take out insurance and take someone up on an offer.

parts.title: Tip: group the meanings
parts.note: Take, get і make мають десятки фразових дієслів, і в одного дієслова часто кілька значень. Групуй їх, як у цьому юніті: фізичне значення (щось справді переміщується) і абстрактне. Для кожного нового значення записуй власний приклад. У таблиці — дієслова з take в обох значеннях; частина прикладів показує значення, яких у цьому юніті немає.

rows: I took the shoes back to the shop.
Sorry, I take it back – your plan is a good one.
He took off without a word. · Take your coat off. · The plane took off late.
The waiter took our plates away.
Take 4 away from 10 and you get 6.
We took in a stray cat.
I was so tired that I didn't take in a word.
The new sofa takes up half the room.
Mum has taken up the piano.
Could you take the rubbish out?
We took out insurance for the trip.

items.pattern: take apart sth / take sth apart · separable; with a pronoun only take it apart (never take apart it) · a clock, a bike, a bed, a wardrobe · opposite: put sth (back) together
items.meaning: separate something into its different pieces, for example to repair it, move it or see how it works
items.example: We had to **take** the wardrobe **apart** to get it out of the bedroom.
more: My nephew **took** the old radio **apart** to see how it worked.
Flat-pack furniture is easy to put together but hard to **take apart**.
items.watchOut: Займенник — тільки посередині: take it apart, а не take apart it. Зібрати назад — put it (back) together. «Розібрати» речі після поїздки — unpack, а не take apart.

items.pattern: take back sth / take sth back (to sb / to the shop) · separable; take it back, never take back it · shoes, a library book, a borrowed drill · a shop takes sth back = agrees to accept it and give you your money back
items.meaning: return something to the shop you bought it from or to the person or place you borrowed it from
items.example: These jeans are too tight, so I'm **taking** them **back** tomorrow.
more: Don't forget to **take back** Olga's umbrella when you see her.
The shop **took** the toaster **back** without any questions.
items.watchOut: Take back — віднести назад від себе, bring back — принести назад до того, хто говорить: Take the books back to the library, але Bring my drill back tomorrow! Return back — тавтологія: або return, або take back.

items.pattern: take sb aside / take aside sb · separable; with a pronoun only take me / her aside (never take aside me) · often + and say / to tell / to ask · also take sb to one side
items.meaning: lead someone away from a group for a moment so that you can talk to them privately
items.example: After the lesson, the teacher **took** me **aside** and asked if everything was all right at home.
more: At my wedding, Grandad **took** me **aside** to give me some advice.
The doctor **took** Mum **aside** and explained the results quietly.
items.watchOut: Людина стоїть посередині: take her aside. Так само кажуть take sb to one side. Не плутай з put sth aside — відкласти (гроші, справу на потім).

items.pattern: no object · informal · take off early / without a word / for the coast · past: took off
items.meaning: leave a place suddenly, often without telling anyone where you are going
items.uk: раптово піти чи поїхати, зірватися з місця
items.example: We were in the middle of dinner when Max suddenly **took off**.
more: When the music stopped, half the guests **took off**.
Sometimes I'd love to **take off** for a week and turn my phone off.
items.watchOut: Розмовне. Take off має й інші значення: літак злітає (The plane took off), зняти одяг (Take off your shoes), стрімко стати успішним (Her business took off). Яке саме значення, видно з контексту.

items.pattern: take up sth / take sth up · separable; take it up · + a hobby, sport or instrument: take up golf, take up the guitar · + -ing: take up running · also take up a job / a post (more formal)
items.meaning: start doing a new activity, especially a hobby or sport, or start a new job
items.example: Last winter my aunt **took up** painting.
more: I've **taken up** running to get fit for the summer.
He'd always loved the guitar and finally **took** it **up** at forty – now he plays in a band.
items.watchOut: Займенник посередині: take it up, а не take up it. Take up ще означає «займати» місце чи час: The bed takes up half the room. Не плутай з be taken up with sth — бути дуже зайнятим чимось (частина C).

items.pattern: take off ten per cent / take ten per cent off (the price / the bill) · separable · an amount of money + off + a price or bill
items.meaning: reduce a price or a total by a certain amount
items.example: The hotel **took** twenty euros **off** our bill because the air conditioning didn't work.
more: If you buy two, they'll **take** 20% **off**.
The baker **took** fifty pence **off** because the bread was from yesterday.
items.watchOut: Ціну знижують так: take £10 off the price, reduce the price або bring the price down; take down тут не підходить. Сума стоїть між take і off або після off: take 10% off / take off 10%.

items.pattern: take away sth / take sth away (from sth) · separable · numbers: take 7 away from 20 · in maths, informal: 20 take away 7 is 13 · formal word: subtract
items.meaning: subtract one number or amount from another
items.example: To work out your change, **take** the price **away** from the amount you paid.
more: **Take away** the cost of the hotel, and we still have £200 for food.
My daughter is good at adding, but **taking away** is harder for her.
items.watchOut: Від якого числа віднімаєш — після from: take 5 away from 12, а не take 5 away of 12. Take away також означає «забрати, прибрати» (take the plates away) і «з собою» про їжу (Eat in or take away? a takeaway).

items.phrase: take sth back (say you were wrong)
items.pattern: take it back / take back what I said / take back everything · separable · about words, not things · often after sorry
items.meaning: say that something you said was wrong and that you didn't mean it
items.example: I said your soup would be boring – I **take it back**, it's delicious.
more: She **took back** everything she'd said about her neighbours.
OK, I **take back** what I said about your driving.
items.watchOut: Найприродніше: I take it back або I take back what I said; слово words тут зайве. Не плутай із take sth back у частині A — повернути річ у магазин.

items.pattern: take in sth / take sth in · separable; take it in · often negative: I didn't take it in · take in the news / information / what sb says / the view / every detail
items.meaning: look at, hear or read something carefully so that you really notice and understand it
items.example: The lecture was so fast that I couldn't **take** it all **in**.
more: On our first day in Rome we just walked around, **taking in** the sights.
She read the letter twice before she really **took in** the news.
items.watchOut: Take in — сприйняти, усвідомити, а не «взяти всередину». «До мене не дійшло» — I didn't take it in. Інші значення: прихистити (take in a stray cat), ушити одяг (take in a dress), обдурити (I was taken in by his story).

items.pattern: take out sth / take sth out · separable · take out insurance / a loan / a mortgage / a subscription / membership
items.meaning: officially arrange to have something such as insurance, a loan or a membership
items.example: We always **take out** travel insurance before a long trip.
more: Lots of young people **take out** a loan to buy their first car.
Our gym is cheaper if you **take out** membership for a whole year.
items.watchOut: «Оформити страховку, кредит» — take out insurance / a loan, а не make insurance. Банківський кредит — a loan, а не a credit. Take out ще означає «винести» (take out the rubbish) і «зводити кудись» (take sb out for dinner).

items.pattern: take to sth / take to doing sth · not separable · after to: a noun or -ing (take to walking, not take to walk) · also take to sb/sth = start to like them
items.meaning: start doing something regularly as a new habit, often because you have come to like it
items.example: Since he got a dog, my dad has **taken to** walking five kilometres a day.
more: Since she retired, Mum has **taken to** phoning me every evening.
Lately our cat has **taken to** sleeping in the bathroom sink.
items.watchOut: Після to — -ing або іменник: take to cycling, не take to cycle. Не плутай з take up — свідомо почати нове хобі; take to — звичка, що з'явилася сама собою, або «вподобати»: The kids took to their new teacher.

items.pattern: be (so / completely) taken up with sth / doing sth · passive form · also sth takes up sb's time
items.meaning: be so busy with something that you have no time or attention for anything else
items.example: This month I'm completely **taken up with** moving house.
more: She's so **taken up with** her new job that she hardly sees her friends.
The whole family is **taken up with** preparations for my sister's wedding.
items.watchOut: Це пасивна форма з прийменником with: I'm taken up with my work. Не плутай з take up sth — почати нове хобі (частина B).

items.pattern: take sb up on an offer / an invitation / it / that · the person goes between take and up: take you up on that · without a person: take up an offer
items.meaning: accept an offer or invitation that someone has made to you
items.example: You said I could stay with you in Lviv – can I **take** you **up on** that?
more: My neighbour offered to water my plants, and I **took** her **up on** it.
Several friends **took** us **up on** our invitation to the barbecue.
items.watchOut: Людина стоїть між take і up, і потрібні обидві частки: I'll take you up on that, а не take up you on that. «Скористатися пропозицією» — не use the offer. Без людини кажуть take up an offer або accept an offer.

items.pattern: sth takes it out of sb · it is fixed · sb = me / you / her … · informal · often really takes it out of you
items.meaning: make someone feel very tired, physically or emotionally
items.example: Looking after a newborn baby really **takes it out of** you.
more: The move **took it out of** all of us.
Two hours of gardening **takes it out of** me these days.
items.watchOut: It — незмінна частина виразу: it takes it out of me, а не it takes out of me. Не плутай з take it out on sb — зганяти злість на комусь: Don't take it out on me!

warmup.uk: Ці черевики замалі, тож я віднесу їх назад у магазин.
warmup.q: These shoes are too small, so I'll ___ to the shop.
warmup.explain: Take sth back — віднести назад. Return back — тавтологія, а займенник стоїть посередині: take them back.

warmup.uk: Вибач, я беру свої слова назад.
warmup.explain: Забрати слова назад — I take it back або I take back what I said. Return my words — калька.
Take up — почати нове хобі. Take over — перебрати керівництво, take after — бути схожим на когось із батьків.

warmup.q: Could you take a bit ___ the price?
warmup.explain: Скинути з ціни — take sth off the price: take £5 off.

warmup.uk: Я був такий втомлений, що до мене не дійшло нічого з того, що він казав.
warmup.q: I was so tired that I didn't ___ anything he said.
warmup.explain: Take in — сприйняти, усвідомити. «До мене не дійшло» — I didn't take it in.

warmup.q: Before the trip we ___ travel insurance.
warmup.explain: Оформити страховку, кредит, абонемент — take out. Можна й get або buy insurance, але не make.

warmup.uk: Якщо твоя пропозиція ще в силі, я нею скористаюся.
warmup.q: If your offer is still open, I'll ___ it.
warmup.explain: Скористатися пропозицією — take sb up on sth. Людина стоїть між take і up, і потрібні обидві частки: up on.

warmup.uk: Ці нічні зміни мене страшенно вимотують.
warmup.explain: Take it out of sb — вимотувати. It тут обов'язкове.

A.q: The bookcase was too big for the stairs, so we had to take it ___.
A.explain: Take sth apart — розібрати на частини.

A.q: Before the meeting, my manager took me ___ and quietly told me about the changes.
A.explain: Take sb aside — відвести вбік, щоб поговорити наодинці.

A.q: One minute Sam was dancing, and the next he'd taken ___ – nobody saw him go.
A.explain: Take off — раптово піти, нікому нічого не сказавши.

B.q: Since he moved to the coast, Dan has taken ___ surfing.

B.explain: Take sth away from sth — відняти одне число від іншого.

B.q: There were so many paintings in the museum that I couldn't take them all ___.
B.explain: Take sth in — сприйняти, роздивитися й усвідомити.

C.q: Since she got a bike, Mia has taken ___ cycling to work.
C.explain: Take to doing sth — взяти за звичку щось робити.

C.q: Kate is so taken up ___ her wedding plans that she never phones anyone.
C.explain: Be taken up with sth — бути повністю зайнятим чимось.

C.q: Painting the whole flat in one weekend really took it ___ us.
C.explain: Take it out of sb — вимотувати, забирати всі сили.

example.title: Dad's new hobby
example.uk:
Коли тато минулої весни вийшов на пенсію, він захопився їздою на велосипеді. Він купив дорогий велосипед і того ж дня оформив на нього страховку. Через тиждень перестали працювати передачі, тож він розібрав велосипед просто на підлозі в кухні. Мама лише похитала головою.

Зібрати його назад тато не зміг, тож відвіз велосипед у магазин частинами. Менеджер відвів його вбік, терпляче вислухав і скинув п'ятдесят фунтів з рахунку за ремонт.

Тепер тато взяв за звичку щоранку проїжджати сорок кілометрів. Це його страшенно вимотує, але йому це дуже подобається. Минулого місяця я сказав йому, що він застарий для цього. Беру свої слова назад — він їздить швидше за мене!
example.en:
When Dad retired last spring, he [[took up|b1]] cycling. He bought an expensive bike and [[took out|c1]] insurance for it the same day. A week later the gears stopped working, so he [[took it apart|a1]] on the kitchen floor. Mum just shook her head.

Dad couldn't put it back together, so he [[took it back|a2]] to the shop in pieces. The manager [[took him aside|a3]], listened patiently and [[took fifty pounds off|b2]] the repair bill.

Now Dad has [[taken to|c2]] riding forty kilometres every morning. It [[takes it out of|c5]] him, but he loves it. Last month I told him he was too old for it. I [[take it back|b4]] – he's faster than me!
